summary:
ws06-audit-verify-signed-manifest-range: audit-verify now checks the manifest signature and can verify sub-range exports. Changes are in cmd/audit-verify only; internal/store and internal/verifier are untouched.

1) Manifest signature. The manifest struct gained generated_at, first_seq, count, first_prev_hash, head_seq, head_hash, key_id and signature. The payload is rebuilt with store.ManifestPayload (imported, not copied) and checked with KeyRing.VerifyPayload. A bad signature exits 2 with a stderr line; an unknown key id exits 3. A manifest with no signature prints "manifest: unsigned" and full-range verdicts are unchanged. This applies to full-range exports too.

2) Sub-range (head_seq > last_seq). Requires a valid signature, otherwise exit 3. Verify runs with FromSeq=first_seq, FromHash=RowHash(first_prev_hash, first row) and Head={last_seq,last_row_hash}. An attestation is passed only when its seq is inside [first_seq,last_seq]. When Verify would report no_attestation, the signed manifest anchors the range instead (verified, or verified_with_legacy). The row count must equal the manifest count, else exit 2 with a stderr line. A range is printed as anchored by the signed manifest only when it verifies.

3) Deviation from the brief. FromHash is not first_prev_hash taken literally: Verify requires FromHash to equal the hash of the FromSeq row itself (verifier.go:349-351), so the literal value would fail every honest sub-range with resume_anchor_mismatch. RowHash(first_prev_hash, first row) binds the start to the signed link; a row with another prev or changed content cannot match (tested).

4) Output. The text report gained a manifest line, and "range end" for sub-ranges. JSON gained a top-level manifest object (supplied, signed, key_id, sub_range, chain_head_seq); verifier.Report fields are unchanged.

5) Tests. 13 new top-level tests, one with 8 tamper subtests (signed full verifies, tamper gives exit 2, unknown key gives exit 3, another key gives exit 2, signed sub-range verifies, unsigned sub-range exit 3, relinked first row, count mismatch, attestation inside a range, checkpoint before/covering the start). The 17 existing tests are unchanged (0 deleted lines in main_test.go).

Open points for the lead: (a) a signed since-only export (last_seq == head_seq, first_seq > 1) still takes the full-range path and reports partial/unanchored_start (never verified); the brief's head_seq > last_seq criterion leaves it there, and widening it would change verdicts for signed full-range inputs. (b) The count-mismatch (exit 2) and checkpoint-covers-start (exit 3) failures print to stderr only, with no JSON report, like the existing input failures. (c) The workflow text said "Files you may edit: (none)", but the packet lists these two files; I followed the packet. (d) Files are LF in both index and worktree, so the CRLF note did not apply.

residual_risks: RedisClaimStore::renew is a GET then a PEXPIRE, so it is not atomic. Inside that window a lapsed claim that has passed to another request can be extended by up to PENDING_TTL. If a Redis outage lasts longer than about 80 s (two missed 40 s ticks), the Pending claim can still lapse. Renewal resumes afterwards but cannot win back a key that another replica has claimed in the meantime.
A stream that never ends now keeps its shared claim for as long as it runs. Only the stream's own deadline bounds this; before, PENDING_TTL did.

It returns false when the key is gone, belongs to another request, or is Done.
